mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months signals an active monetary easing policy that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS has declined for at least 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 7.0% for two consecutive months, it signals a severe labor market contraction that typically precedes a recession, causing equity markets to anticipate reduced corporate earnings and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE has exceeded 7.0% for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate and an increase in the unemployment rate signals a central bank's aggressive response to a deepening recession, which typically triggers a short-term equity market rebound as investors anticipate fiscal and monetary stimulus, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS declines > 0.4pp and UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in 3 months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 55% of instances meeting the trigger condition, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In the post-financial crisis recovery phase, a sustained increase in residential construction permits (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average signals improving consumer confidence and housing market strength, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as the economy transitions to a new expansion.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is negative in more than 55% of instances during the post-financial crisis recovery phase when RSAFS is above its 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) over the past 3 months indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 55% of instances where PAYEMS has increased for at least 3 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 650,000 units per month for two consecutive months, it signals a robust housing market that drives consumer confidence and economic growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is negative in more than 55% of instances where HOUST has exceeded 650.0 for two consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) signals a broad-based economic recovery, where both consumer demand and business investment are strengthening, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises > 0.5% and INDPRO rises > 0.3% in 3 months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 55% of instances meeting the trigger condition, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a supply shock regime characterized by declining industrial production (INDPRO) and rising input costs (CPIAUCSL), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 60 trading days due to stagflationary pressures and reduced corporate profit margins.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in more than 55% of instances during the supply shock regime (defined as INDPRO < 100 and CPIAUCSL > 2.0% YoY), or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
